title: Payment of Tax
outcomes: Explain the electronic ledgers and modes of deposit.
Apply the order of discharge and payment due dates.
Compute interest on delayed payment and wrong ITC.

meta.exam_tip: In interest sums, check whether the base is the cash portion and whether ITC was actually utilised.

concepts.title: Electronic ledgers and modes of payment (s. 49)
body: Each registered person has three electronic records on the portal: the cash ledger (deposits), the credit ledger (ITC) and the liability register (all dues).

Deposits into the cash ledger use a challan (valid 15 days) paid by internet banking, debit or credit card, NEFT/RTGS, UPI or over the counter (up to ₹10,000 per challan per period); the date of credit to the Government account is the date of deposit.

The cash ledger pays tax, interest, penalty, fees and other amounts; the credit ledger pays only output tax. Amounts can be transferred between heads in the cash ledger and, for CGST and IGST, to a distinct person with the same PAN. Unused balances in the cash ledger can be refunded.
concepts.analogy: Cash is the universal key; credit opens only the output-tax door.
concepts.work: A trader with ₹5 lakh of ITC must still pay a ₹2,000 late fee in cash.

concepts.title: Order of discharge and due dates
body: Section 49(8) order: first, self-assessed tax and other dues for previous periods; then the current period; then any amount payable under a demand (sections 73 or 74).

Due dates: monthly filers pay by the 20th of the next month with GSTR-3B. Quarterly (QRMP) filers pay for the first two months by the 25th of the following month (either 35% of last quarter's cash tax, or actual tax), and for the quarter with GSTR-3B by the 22nd or 24th depending on the State.
Reverse charge tax is paid in cash. TDS and TCS deducted by others are credited to the cash ledger of the supplier once accepted.
concepts.analogy: Old dues are cleared before new ones, so a short payment always shows up as a current-period default.
concepts.work: A QRMP taxpayer with low sales in April may pay actual tax by 25 May instead of 35% of the earlier quarter's cash.

concepts.title: Interest on delayed payment (s. 50)
body: Section 50(1): interest at 18% a year on tax not paid by the due date, from the day after the due date until payment. Where the return is filed late but before proceedings, interest is on the cash portion only.

Section 50(3): where ITC is wrongly availed and utilised, interest is payable at the notified rate (18%) from the date of utilisation to the date of reversal or payment; credit merely availed but not used attracts no interest.
ITC is treated as utilised when the balance in the credit ledger falls below the wrongly availed amount. Interest is paid in cash and is not deductible from ITC.
concepts.analogy: Interest charges only for the time the Government was actually short of cash.
concepts.work: Wrong credit of ₹10,000 sitting unused in the ledger costs nothing; once used, interest starts.

illustrations.title: Paying late
illustrations.q: For a month, Kavi Industries (monthly filer) had output tax of ₹1,00,000, of which ₹60,000 was set off by ITC and ₹40,000 was payable in cash. It filed GSTR-3B and paid 30 days after the due date. Separately, it had wrongly availed and used ITC of ₹25,000, reversed 73 days later. Compute interest (round to the nearest rupee).

solution.text: Interest on late payment is on the net cash liability where the return is filed before any proceedings begin.

jobs.title: Payment calendar for a QRMP client
jobs.situation: A small trader on QRMP keeps missing the monthly payment.
steps: Explain the 25th deadline for months one and two.
Generate challan early; it is valid 15 days.
jobs.takeaway: Quarterly returns still mean monthly payments.

mcqs.q: Late fee under GST can be paid from:
mcqs.explain: The credit ledger pays only output tax; fees, interest and penalties are paid in cash. In practice: keep cash for these.
mcqs.topic: Electronic ledgers and modes of payment (s. 49)

mcqs.q: A GST challan is valid for:
mcqs.explain: A challan generated on the portal must be paid within 15 days. In practice: generate it close to payment.
mcqs.topic: Electronic ledgers and modes of payment (s. 49)

mcqs.q: Over-the-counter payment is allowed up to:
mcqs.explain: Cash or cheque payments at the bank counter are capped at ₹10,000 per challan per period (with exceptions for Government recoveries). In practice: use online modes.
mcqs.topic: Electronic ledgers and modes of payment (s. 49)

mcqs.q: Which dues are discharged first under section 49(8)?
mcqs.explain: Order: previous periods, then current period, then demands. In practice: arrears eat into current payments.
mcqs.topic: Order of discharge and due dates

mcqs.q: Monthly payment under QRMP for the first two months of a quarter is due by:
mcqs.explain: QRMP taxpayers deposit by the 25th using Form PMT-06. In practice: the fixed-sum option is 35% of last quarter's cash tax.
mcqs.topic: Order of discharge and due dates

mcqs.q: Interest on delayed payment of tax is:
mcqs.explain: Section 50(1) and the notification set 18% per annum. In practice: compute by days.

mcqs.q: Interest on ITC wrongly availed applies when:
mcqs.explain: Section 50(3) charges interest only on credit both availed and utilised. In practice: reverse early.

mcqs.q: For a return filed late (no proceedings), interest is charged on:
options: The cash portion of the tax
mcqs.explain: The proviso to section 50(1) limits interest to the part paid in cash. In practice: ITC available in the ledger reduces the base.

summary: Cash ledger, credit ledger, liability register.
Credit ledger: output tax only; RCM, interest, fees, penalty in cash.
Monthly by 20th; QRMP months by 25th (35% or actual).
Interest 18%; on cash portion; wrong ITC only if utilised.
remember: Challan valid 15 days; OTC up to ₹10,000.
traps: Merely availed wrong ITC: no interest.
TDS/TCS credit goes to cash ledger.

viva.q: What is the electronic liability register?
viva.model: The portal record of all amounts payable by a taxpayer — tax, interest, penalty, fee — and how they are discharged.

viva.q: What can the credit ledger pay?
viva.model: Only output tax; interest, penalty, fees and reverse charge tax must be paid from the cash ledger.

viva.q: What is the order of discharge?
viva.model: Previous periods' self-assessed dues, then the current period, then demands raised under sections 73 or 74.

viva.q: When is interest charged on ITC?
viva.model: When ITC is wrongly availed and utilised, at 18% from utilisation till reversal.

viva.q: What is the date of deposit in the cash ledger?
viva.model: The date on which the amount is credited to the Government account in the authorised bank, as shown by the challan identification number.

cases.title: Bloom Florists
cases.case: Bloom Florists, a QRMP taxpayer, had cash tax of ₹20,000 in the last quarter. For April it chooses the fixed-sum method. It has ITC of ₹30,000 but owes a late fee of ₹1,000 and reverse charge tax of ₹4,000 on rent.

mcqs.q: April payment under the fixed-sum method:
mcqs.explain: 35% of last quarter's cash tax: 35% × ₹20,000 = ₹7,000, due by 25 May. In practice: it is adjusted in the quarterly return.
mcqs.topic: Order of discharge and due dates

mcqs.q: The late fee is paid from:
mcqs.explain: Fees are paid only in cash. In practice: ITC cannot pay fees.
mcqs.topic: Electronic ledgers and modes of payment (s. 49)

mcqs.q: Reverse charge tax on rent is paid from:
mcqs.explain: RCM tax must be paid in cash. In practice: it can then be claimed as ITC.
mcqs.topic: Electronic ledgers and modes of payment (s. 49)

mcqs.q: If Bloom pays the quarter's tax 10 days late on a cash liability of ₹18,250, interest is:
mcqs.explain: ₹18,250 × 18% × 10/365 = ₹90. In practice: interest is in cash.
